Product link: http://www.amazon.com/Bluedio-Legend-Version-Bluetooth-Headset/dp/B00LJWEKNG/ref=sr_1_5?ie=UTF8&qid=1437506131&sr=8-5&keywords=bluedio+wireless+legend

Bluedio Legend+ headphones. I see a lot of people all over the internet ask for a great product suggestion for wireless, over the ear headphones, so I am here to suggest one. I own these, and have put them through their paces for a solid year. Wearing them almost every day at the gym (weights and cardio) for I'd wager a total of 340 total "wears" and approx 45minutes to 2 hours per wear. So yes, I have worn them quite a bit.

You're familiar with Beats headphones and the like, but don't enjoy paying the high price? Check these out instead and save some money. I am no sort of paid spokesman, just a guy who owns Sennheiser, Sony, Logitech, and Able Planet headphones and will tell you that these Bluedio's are the best of the bunch.

Very great quality audio, super comfortable and the battery lasts a long time per full charge (i'm guessing 2x as long as the Beats). NFC, wired, and get this.. also has a space for a MicroSD card for those times you don't want to go wireless/wired to a source. I have tried the MicroSD and yes, it just works simple as can be.

Skip forward/back on the headphone, audio up and down as well. Very well made, sturdy, but not heavy. All kinds of color options as well, and additionally, these are on the higher end of headphones from Bluedio, there are lower tier versions that seem to be on par overall with the Legend+ line. also, there is a newer "highest" end line, still only $200.00 USD.

I wouldn't be a fair judge if I didn't mention a few cons:

They can make your ears rather warm during intense workouts, however for usual workouts, I have been fine.

Every so often (30 or so uses), I may have a time when I fast forward on my phone or the headphones themselves, and the song doesn't go forward right away. It may take a few seconds to jump to the next song. I am 95% sure that's my 3yr old android phone though. Even if it's not, it's hardly a huge issue at all.

Doesn't come with a case, some Beats/other headphones might come with a hard clamshell case

Takeaway:

Cheaper than most every rival

More features than similar headphones that cost hundreds more

Comfortable

Long battery life

Very stylish

NFC

Great bass, clear treble, songs sound like they should

Very strong bluetooth signal, can reach across a basketball court + weight equipment WITHOUT a clear line of sight

Wired or wireless

MicroSD card slot for the times you don't want or don't have your phone/iPod/tablet available

On headphone controls for both Bluetooth and MicroSD card use.. 2 separate control centers depending on what your source is.

Lego movie worked because Lego isn't a plot, it's just a material that everything in the universe happens to be made out of.

Minecraft: The Movie is intrinsically a bit more restrictive, because Minecraft already has a plot of sorts. Guy digs up shit and uses it to build other shit.

Also, Minecraft has a distinctive visual style. If they keep it, it's just going to look like shitty machinima, and I don't think people want to look at that for 90 minutes on a big screen. If they lose it, it's no longer Minecraft.

Finally, Lego has a huge built-in audience of all ages, everybody in the first world is pretty familiar with Lego, even the tiny minority who have never played with it. Minecraft is very successful for what it is, but the total number of people who have played Minecraft is still tiny compared to the Lego audience.

Um this is dumb. Sounds like they want to make a movie based on every aspect of life np matter how fucking dumb it is.

It isn't that dumb. If they made Omelettes: The Movie I'd agree, but Minecraft is probably the most culturally relevant video game to make an impact on the mainstream since Pokemon. As a cynical adult, I want to roll my eyes, but look at the success of the Lego Movie.

But Minecraft (to my knowledge) doesn't really have a story. It's a sand box game with an optional survival mode. Yes, millions play it but there's nothing unique about it. It's only real hook is the editable voxel based environment. But to base a movie on minecraft voxels will just look like a movie with shitty CGI. But Legos are just 3D blocks you say? Yes, but the level of detail used in that movie to render all those blocks is phenomenal. The CGI is top notch in simulating a world made from a whole slew of varied lego pieces. Voxels in mincraft are just arbitrary cubes with low res textures. They are a technical compromise needed in order to support the sand box nature of the game. A movie can't capture that sandbox nature and thus you're just left with ugly cubes. I guess if they have a kick ass funny script nobody will care but in that case I'd rather see that script made into a lego movie....
That's all true, but no excited little kid is going to care. Maybe The Lego Movie is the wrong comparison to make here.

The other thing about Lego was the Lego Movie wasn't their first foray into the entertainment business. They had produced a series of TV shows and direct to DVD movies before tackling "The Movie".

I think it would serve Minecraft better if they produced a series of webisodes first to get a feel for what works rather than jumping straight into a major motion picture. Or maybe they have (I don't follow the game that closely). Then again, when you have the money Mojang has, caution takes a whole different meaning :).
